questions.question: Plasma is often called the ______ state of matter.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**fourth.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plasma** is often called the **fourth state of matter** because it has **unique properties** that distinguish it from the other** three states** (solid, liquid, and gas).
 
• Plasma is a state of matter in which a** gas is ionized, **meaning that some or all of its** atoms** have **lost or gained electrons.**
 
• This creates a mixture of** positively charged ions** and** negatively charged electrons **that can conduct** electricity **and respond to** magnetic fields.**
 
• Plasma is found in many natural and artificial environments, including **lightning, stars, flames, **and some types of** lamps.**
 
• It can also be** created in laboratories** by heating or applying **electric fields to gases.**
 
• Plasma has several practical applications, such as in **plasma cutting and welding, plasma TVs and displays**, and **plasma thrusters** for **spacecraft.**
 
• The idea of plasma as a distinct state of matter was first proposed by the** American physicist Irving Langmuir **in the **1920s,** based on his studies of **electric discharges in gases.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• Ninth and eighth are **not correct** because there are only **four known states of matter,** not nine or eight.

 
 
• However, some scientists have proposed **additional states or sub-states of matter** based on different criteria, such as **quark-gluon plasma or Bose-Einstein condensates.**
 
 
 
• **Sixth** is also **incorrect** because there are only four states of matter, not six.

questions.question: Who among the following was the last Pallava king?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Aparajitavarman. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aparajitavarman** was the **last Pallava king.**
 
• The **Pallava dynasty** ruled in **Southern India** from the **3rd to the 9th century CE.**
 
• **Simha Vishnu **was the **founder** of the Pallava dynasty.
 
• **Narasimhavarman I** was one of the most powerful kings of the dynasty who is known for his patronage of the** arts and architecture.**
 
• **Mahendra Varma** was another prominent king of the Pallava dynasty who is known for his **military conquests** and the construction of several temples.
 
• **Aparajitavarman** was the** last king** of the dynasty who ruled from** 880 to 897 CE.** 
 
• He was succeeded by the **Chola dynasty**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• The **Pallava dynasty **was known for its patronage of the** arts, literature, and architecture.**
 
• The** rock-cut temples at Mahabalipuram **and the** Shore Temple in Mamallapuram **are some of the finest examples of Pallava architecture.
 
• **Mahendravarman I **was the** first Pallava king **who established his capital at** Kanchipuram.**
 
 
• He is credited with the construction of the **Kailasanatha temple.**
 
 
 
• **Narasimhavarman I **is known for his **military conquests**, including the defeat of the **Chalukya king Pulakeshin II**, and his patronage of the arts and **architecture.**
 
 
• He is credited with the construction of the **Shore Temple **and the** Five Rathas at Mahabalipuram.**
 
 
 
• **Simhavishnu **was a powerful king who is known for his **military conquests**, including the **annexation of the Chera and Chola** kingdoms.
 
 
• He is credited with the construction of several temples, including the **Vaikuntha Perumal temple** and the **Muktheeswarar temple.**

questions.question: In October 2022, ISRO chairman announced expected launch year of Chandrayaan 3 in ______.

__
 
• **ISRO chairman **announced that **Chandrayaan 3** is expected to be launched in **2023, **which is **two years later **than its initial planned launch year of **2021.**
 
• **Chandrayaan 3** is the** third lunar exploration mission** by the **Indian Space Research Organisation** (ISRO).
 
• It is aimed at conducting further studies on the **Moon's surface**, particularly in the **south polar region**, where** water molecules **have been detected.
 
• **Option 1**, i.e., 2030, is** incorrect** as it is too far away from the expected launch year.
 
• **Option 2**, i.e., 2027, and **option 3,** i.e., 2025, are also **incorrect** as they are not the exact launch year announced by the ISRO chairman.

• Chandrayaan 2 aimed to make a** soft landing on the Moon's south polar region** but had a **communication failure** during the final stages of landing.

questions.question: What is the study of interactions between a living organism and its environment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ecology.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ecology** is the study of interactions between **living organisms **and their** environment.**
 
• It is a **branch of biology **that deals with the **study of organisms **and their** surroundings.**
 
• It encompasses a wide range of topics, including the **distribution and abundance of organisms,** the **functioning of ecosystems,** and the **impact of human activities **on the environment.
 
• Ecologists study the **relationships **between organisms and their environment at different levels, from individual organisms to entire ecosystems.
 
• The goal of ecology is to understand how organisms** interact with each other** and with their environment, and how these interactions** shape** the **structure and function of ecosystems.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biome:** A biome is a **large,** naturally occurring **community of plants** and **animals** that occupy a **major habitat.**

 
 
• Biomes are characterized by their** climate, vegetation, and other abiotic factors**.
 
 
 
• **Bio-reserve**: A biosphere reserve is a **protected area **that aims to **conserve biodiversity** while promoting **sustainable development.**
 
 
• Biosphere reserves are designated by **UNESCO **and typically include** core areas, buffer zones, and transition zones.**
 
 
 
• **Ecosystem**: An ecosystem is a **community of living organisms **and their **physical environment**, which includes both **biotic and abiotic factors.**
 
 
• **​**Ecosystems can range in size from** small ponds to entire biomes.**
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is** option 1.**

questions.question: Sangphao tribal dance is performed in which of the following states?

questions.question: Which continent of the world is referred to as a “Continent, Dedicated to Science”?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Antarctica.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Antarctica** is referred to as a** "Continent, Dedicated to Science"** due to its** unique environment **and the presence of **numerous scientific research stations.**
 
• The continent is home to the **South Pole Telescope **and the **IceCube Neutrino Observatory**, among other research facilities.
 
• Scientists conduct studies on topics such as** climate change, glaciology, and astrobiology **in Antarctica.
 
• The continent is governed by the** Antarctic Treaty System**, which outlines guidelines for **scientific research and environmental protection.**
 
• Other options, such as **Africa, North America, and Asia**, are not referred to as a "Continent, Dedicated to Science," although they are home to a number of **scientific research institutions **and initiatives.
 
• Hence, the **correct option **for the given question is **option 2, Antarctica.**

questions.question: In which of the following parts of the Indian constitution, Fundamental Rights are contained?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part III.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fundamental Rights **are enshrined in **Part III **of the Indian Constitution.
 
• **Part IV **deals with** Directive Principles of State Policy.**
 
• **Part II ** deals with the** Union, its territory, citizenship, a**nd related provisions.
 
• The Constitution deals with citizenship from Articles 5 to 11 under Part II.
 
• **Fundamental Rights** are considered as the **basic human right**s that are guaranteed to every citizen of India.
 
• These rights are based on the principles of **equality, liberty, and fraternity.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Part IV **of the Indian Constitution deals with Directive Principles of State Policy, which are **non-justiciable guidelines or principles **for the government to follow while making **laws and policies.**
 
• **Part II** of the Indian Constitution deals with **Citizenship**
 
• **Fundamental Rights** are considered as one of the **most important features **of the Indian Constitution and they ensure that every citizen of India has the right to **equality, freedom, and justice.**

questions.question: Who was the Governor - General of India when Doctrine of Lapse was introduced in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Dalhousie.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Doctrine of Lapse** was introduced by **Lord Dalhousie,** who was the **Governor-General of India **from **1848 to 1856.**
 
• The doctrine allowed the **British East India Company** to **take over the territories **of Indian rulers who died without a** male heir.**
 
• Lord Dalhousie implemented this policy in order to** expand British control **over India and to **eliminate **the local rulers who were seen as **obstacles to British rule.**
 
• The Doctrine of Lapse was highly **controversial** and led to widespread **resentment **among Indian rulers and their subjects.
 
• **Lord Mountbatten** was the **last British Governor-General of India,** who oversaw the transfer of power to India in **1947**.
 
• **Lord Cornwallis** was the **Governor-General of Bengal ,** who served from **1786 to 1793.**
 
• **Lord Canning** was the Governor-General of India during the **Indian Rebellion of 1857.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Mountbatten **was appointed as the** Governor-General of India in 1947**, and he played a key role in the **transfer of power** from the **British to the Indian government.**
 
• **Lord Cornwallis** was a **British military commander** who served as the Governor-General of India during a period of significant **British expansion** in India. 
 
 
• He is also known for his role in the** American War of Independence.**
 
 
 
• **Lord Canning** was the Governor-General of India during the Indian Rebellion of **1857**, which was a major uprising against British rule in India. 
 
 
• He is remembered for his efforts to **restore peace and order **in the aftermath of the rebellion.
 
 
 
• Hence, the** correct answer** is option 2, Lord Dalhousie.

questions.question: Presence of which phenomenon leads to weakening of trade winds in a region?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**El Nino.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **El Nino** is a phenomenon that leads to **weakening of trade winds** in a region.
 
• During El Nino, the** sea surface temperatures** in the Pacific Ocean near the Equator become **warmer **than usual, which affects the** atmospheric circulation **and leads to weakening of trade winds.
 
• Trade winds are the **prevailing easterly winds** that blow towards the **Equator in the tropics**, and they are important for **navigation and weather patterns.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Coriolis force **is a phenomenon that influences the** direction of winds and ocean currents**, but it does not directly lead to weakening of trade winds.
 
• **Mango Shower** is a **meteorological phenomenon** that occurs in some parts of India during the **pre-monsoon season**, and it is not related to trade winds. 
 
• **La Nina** is a phenomenon that is opposite to **El Nino,** and it leads to **strengthening of trade winds** in a region.
 
• Hence, the statement "Presence of which phenomenon leads to weakening of trade winds in a region?" is **correctly answered** by option 3, El Nino.

questions.question: The mode of nutrition in which organisms make food themselves from simple substances is called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**autotrophic nutrition.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Autotrophic nutrition** is the mode of nutrition in which organisms make their** food themselves **from simple substances.
 
• The process of autotrophic nutrition involves the use of** light energy **(in photosynthesis) or **chemical energy **(in chemosynthesis) to **produce organic compounds.**
 
• Autotrophs are organisms that carry out** autotrophic nutrition**, such as **plants, algae, and some bacteria**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Heterotrophic** nutrition is the mode of nutrition in which organisms obtain their **food by consuming **other organisms or organic matter.
 
• **Saprotrophic **nutrition is a type of heterotrophic nutrition in which organisms obtain their food by **decomposing dead organic matter.**
 
• **Phototrophic **nutrition is a subcategory of autotrophic nutrition, in which organisms use** light energy** to produce their** own food.**

questions.question: Which of the following soil requires minimum tillage because of its self-cultivating feature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Black soil.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Black soil** is also known as **regur soil or black cotton soil.**
 
• It is found in the **Deccan plateau** and is particularly well-suited for** growing cotton crops.**
 
• It has a **high clay content**, which makes it highly **retentive of moisture** and **nutrients.**
 
• This means that it requires **less frequent irrigation and fertilization, **which in turn reduces the need for **tilling and weeding.**
 
• The **high clay content** also makes **black soil heavy** and** difficult to plow**, which is why it is often referred to as** "sticky" soil.**
 
• However, this also means that it is** highly stable **and** resistant to erosion.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Peaty soil** (option 3) is a type of soil that is characterized by a **high organic content.** 

 
 
• It is found in **wetlands and marshes** and is** not suitable **for agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Laterite soil** (option 2) is a type of soil that is formed in** tropical and subtropical regions.** 
 
 
• It is highly weathered and has a **high iron and aluminum content**. 
 
• It is** not suitable **for agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Red soil** (option 1) is a type of soil that is** commonly **found in India. 
 
 
• It is formed from the **weathering of igneous rocks** and has a **reddish color** due to the presence of** iron oxide.** 
 
• It is suitable for growing crops like **pulses, millets, and oilseeds.**
 
 
 
• Hence, the statement "The **correct answer** is option 4" is correct.

questions.question: Chandragupta, was the first ruler of the Gupta dynasty to adopt the grand title of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** maharaj-adhiraja.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Maharaj-adhiraja" **means "**king of kings"** or **"emperor"**, which was a **grand title **adopted by **Chandragupta, **the first ruler of the Gupta dynasty.
 
• Option 1, **"dharamraja**", means **"king of dharma"** or "**king of righteousness"**, which was a title used by some Indian rulers, but not by Chandragupta.
 
• Option 3, **"maharaja"**, means **"king" or "great king",** which was a common title for Indian rulers, but not as grand as "maharaj-adhiraja".
 
• Option 4, "**devanampriya",** means **"beloved of the gods"**, which was a title used by Emperor Ashoka, but not by Chandragupta.
 
• Hence, the statement is **correct **that Chandragupta was the first ruler of the Gupta dynasty to adopt the grand title of** "maharaj-adhiraja".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• From the beginning of the** fourth century CE** to the beginning of the **sixth century CE**, the **Gupta Empire **ruled over ancient India.
 
• The Gupta empire was **started** by** Chandra Gupta I**, the first monarch of India.
 
• The **final **of the great Gupta emperors is typically regarded as **Skandagupta**, the son and successor of Kumaragupta I.

questions.question: Which Indian monument was the most visited monument by domestic tourists in financial year 2022?

• It is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site **and is known for its intricate design and beautiful architecture.

questions.question: Which architectural style of India was distinguished by the use of overhanging balconies and arched cornices?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The **Rajput style of architecture** is known for its unique **cornices and balconies,** which give it a distinct identity.
 
• The use of **meharaabs**, which are **decorative niches** in the walls of **mosques**, is also a characteristic feature of **Rajput architecture.**
 
• The Rajput style flourished in the **medieval period in Rajastha**n and other parts of northern India.
 
• This style was influenced by both **Hindu and Islamic architectural traditions**, and is known for its intricate **carvings and ornamentation.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sikh architecture** is characterized by its **simplicity and emphasis** on **functionality, rather than decoration.**

 
 
• The **Golden Temple in Amritsar** is a prime example of Sikh architecture.
 
 
 
• **Nagara style of architecture** is prevalent in **North India** and is known for its **tall and curvilinear spires,** called **shikhara,** on the top of temples.
 
• **Mughal architecture **is known for its** grandeur **and use of **white marble and red sandstone**. 
 
 
• The Taj Mahal is a classic example of **Mughal architecture.**

questions.question: In hockey, yellow card refers to temporary suspension of player for a minimum of ______ minutes of playing time.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**five.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A** yellow card in hockey** refers to a **warning **given to a player for a **minor offense.**
 
• If a player receives a yellow card, they are **temporarily suspended** from the game for a** minimum of five minutes** of playing time.
 
• During this time, the player's team must play with **one less player on the ice.**
 
• If the player commits** another offense** and receives a **second yellow card**, they will be given a **red card** and **permanently expelled** from the game.
 
• Other options mentioned in the question, such as **three, seven, or nine minutes,** are** incorrect** and do not correspond to the standard rules of hockey.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ice Hockey** is a popular sport **played on ice,** with** two teams of six players **each trying to score goals by hitting a small puck into the opposing team's net.
 
• The game is known for its** physicality and high-speed action**, with players wearing protective gear such as **helmets, pads, and gloves**.
 
• In addition to yellow and red cards, referees may also use **hand signals** to indicate penalties such as** slashing, tripping, or hooking.**
 
• These penalties can result in a player being** temporarily or permanently suspended** from the game, depending on the** severity of the offense **and the number of previous warnings or penalties.

questions.question: When a person moves to a new country, it is called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** immigration.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Immigration** is a process where a person** enters a new country** with the intent to** settle there permanently **or for an** extended period.**
 
• People may immigrate for various reasons such as **job opportunities, better living standards, education, etc.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 2, (Emigration) **refers to the act of **leaving one's own country** to settle permanently or for an extended period in another country.
 
• It is the** opposite of immigration.**
 
• **Option 3, (Out - Migration)** refers to the movement of people from **one region or country to another** in search of **better opportunities or living conditions.**
 
• **Option 4, (Intra - Migration)** refers to the movement of people **within the same country or region**, usually from rural to urban areas, in search of **better opportunities or living conditions.**
 
• Therefore, the** correct answer** is option 1, (Immigration).

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__****Difference b/n Immigration and Emigration :**

 
• Immigration and emigration** are different in terms of the direction and perspective of the movement.**
 
• **Immigration** means moving **into a new country,** while** emigration** means moving **out of a country**.
 
• For** example**, if a person leaves India and settles in Canada, they are an immigrant from the perspective of Canada and an emigrant from the perspective of India .
 
• **Immigration and emigration **are both **forms of migration**, which is the general term for the movement of people from one place to another.
